images.title: Ends or repeats?
images.purpose: Recap the topic's test: run the long division and watch the remainder; 0 means it ends, a returning remainder means it repeats.
images.composition: One start box at the top centre branching to two outcome cards, left and right; generous white space.
exact_structure: Top centre: one grey #6B7280 outlined box with the text watch the remainder.
Two arrows down from it: left arrow labelled remainder 0, right arrow labelled remainder comes back.
Left card, green #009E73 outline: ends, with the example 1 ÷ 8 = 0.125 below it.
Right card, vermilion #D55E00 outline: repeats for ever, with the example 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666... below it.
rejection: the ending example not 0.125 or the repeating example not 0.666...
the examples swapped between the two cards
images.takeaway: If a remainder becomes 0 the quotient ends; if a remainder comes back, its digits repeat for ever.
images.description: A box saying watch the remainder branches to ends, with 1 ÷ 8 = 0.125, and repeats for ever, with 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666...
images.context: Shown beside the practice task on deciding whether a division ends.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to trace each example's remainders to see which branch it takes.

image_decisions.why: A two branch recap captures the topic's single test.
